findings.title: Two authorization styles coexist, bridged by overwriting the JWT user claim
findings.detail:
The original design, where the browser calls PostgREST under RLS and functions read auth.uid(), was partly replaced on 2026-09-08 (20260908132000_harden_public_function_execute_privileges.sql) by API -> service_role -> function(actor_user_id). The switch was never finished:
- 39 functions still use auth.uid().
- 45 functions overwrite the JWT user claim (set_config('request.jwt.claim.sub', actor_user_id)) so that auth.uid()-based inner functions see the actor. Example: save_employee_service -> save_employee.
- 8 SELECT policies on employee_* tables are dead (no grant).
- The web still reads about 15 settings/reference tables directly under RLS.
Result: the same rule has to hold in RLS policies, in auth.uid() functions, in actor functions and in the API gate.
findings.fix_shape: Pick one style: actor parameter + service_role, with the API as the only entry point. Move the web's direct reads behind the API (or keep RLS on those reference tables using the same predicate). Delete the claim bridge and the dead policies. This is part of the class-2 rebuild.

findings.title: No single authorization predicate; 16 separate location-scope implementations that disagree
findings.detail:
There are 16 boolean helpers that implement location scope, about 20 domain helpers (service_actor_has_permission, schedule_actor_has_capability_service, service_actor_can_time_location and others) and 15 API authorize() functions. Differences verified by reading code:
- `target_location_id is null` passes in the schedule helpers.
- document_actor_blocked is checked in can_access_location and service_actor_has_permission but not in the schedule helpers.
- Role comes from membership.role in one helper (with a hardcoded employee allowlist) and from access_class in another.
- The important_dates read policy ignores location.
BL-070 evidence: the manager-terminate regression (the membership trigger was rewritten twice on the same day and the second rewrite dropped the manager branch), plus the ANY vs ALL rule split listed in G's table (person drawer uses ANY, old availability approval uses ALL).
findings.fix_shape: One `authorize(actor, workspace, action, target)` with target in {workspace, location, person, shift}, encoding M2 once: person uses the ANY-location rule, a shift belongs to its location, cross-location actions need per-location votes, and managers act only on the employee rank. Replace all helpers and wrappers, delete the rest. Add a generated authorization-matrix pgTAP: 4 roles × in-scope/out-of-scope × 75 permission keys. Estimate 3–5 person-weeks.

findings.title: pgTAP is not a CI gate; 38 red files built up unseen
findings.detail: ci.yml runs lint/typecheck/test/build only. The structural guards (tenant_owned_composite_foreign_keys, function_execute_privileges) had already caught the 11 FKs and 1 browser-exposed definer function, but they were red and nobody saw them. 13 of the 31 red files outside Line Up are only out-of-date tests. The previous generation's brief also asked for these tests. Without a CI gate, any rebuild drifts the same way.
findings.fix_shape: Add `supabase start && supabase test db` to CI before any rebuild work; delete tests that describe retired models (the 5 green availability files named by D2, and others). Estimate 0.5 person-weeks. This is a precondition for every option.

findings.title: Plan-edit lock is per workspace + week, and taking over a session wipes another location's draft
findings.detail: Verified: `schedule_edit_sessions_active_week_idx` UNIQUE (workspace_id, week_start) WHERE status='active'. BL-070/G re-ran it: an admin takes over a manager's session, and on save another location's draft shifts are silently deleted. This is a class-1 table that encodes the wrong scope granularity. It is the one domain-model defect that loses data.
findings.fix_shape: Lock per (workspace, week, location set) and make save touch only the session's locations (G's D3). Needed under any option, including a full rebuild. Moderate risk, about 0.5–1 person-week.

findings.title: Parallel and half-finished systems: 36 tables, nothing ever deleted
findings.detail:
- Old availability: 8 tables (employee_schedule_availability_versions and others), about 74 functions. The Schedule grid still reads it through get_schedule_read_model_service_label_base, while save and publish use the new weekly-preference system. There are 4 live readers.
- Legacy shift-change requests: 3 tables, parallel to Shift Hub's 5. The Shift Hub flag `shift_exchanges_enabled` defaults to false and has no API; the manager's Shift Hub view was removed on Sep 14.
- Kiosk (6) and time tracking (8): 14 tables, outside the MVP, forbidden by the rebuild brief, yet back in the schema.
- Line Up: 11 tables awaiting simplification.
- The notification platform (16 tables) has producers without recipients (preferred name).
findings.fix_shape:
Decide and delete:
- BL-091 removal in D2's order (port the 4 readers, remove the lock trigger, drop tables, functions and tests): 1–1.5 person-weeks, risky.
- Shift Hub vs legacy Requests, removing the flag and restoring manager approval: 1–1.5 person-weeks.
- Delete or freeze kiosk and time tracking: 0.5 person-weeks.
- Line Up: separate decision.

findings.title: Accumulated layering and legacy tolerance
findings.detail:
- 36 `_base` wrapper layers (2,365 lines) in about 6 wrapper chains; mutate_schedule_edit_shift_service is 5 deep.
- 407 function rewrites across migrations.
- 3 tombstones (save_employee_availability_service, save_employee_hub_availability_service, confirm_employee_document_service).
- 11 _v2/_v3 functions and about 20–30 functions with no production caller.
- Duplicate settings (availability_warning_policy / availability_enforcement / conflict_policy next to conflict_rules, synced by a trigger).
- app_private.bl051_* snapshot tables and notification_legacy_default_accounts.
- The 'unknown shift time' states (legacy_unverified).
BL-070 bugs that live here: the preferred-name wipe (the wrapper passes ''), and BL-092 (the shared evaluator is not given the exclusion list).
findings.fix_shape: Collapse each wrapper chain into one function, delete tombstones, orphans, versions and duplicate columns, then squash 319 migrations into a dump-derived baseline (about 55k lines) and re-verify the seed, the local fixture and the hosted DB (no live data). Estimate 1.5–2.5 person-weeks.

findings.title: Web and API are tightly coupled to the plpgsql JSON shapes
findings.detail: API services call the RPC and parse the result with a shared zod schema (for example employee-hub-service.ts: scheduleReadModelSchema.parse). 439 schemas have 1,321 snake_case keys, and 168 web files make 3,495 snake_case reads (.employee_id 167, .week_start 146, .location_id 129 and so on). Any rebuild that changes RPC output shapes ripples into the web.
findings.fix_shape: In the targeted option, keep RPC signatures and output shapes stable and change only preambles and internals, so web impact is near zero apart from the intended UI changes. In a full rebuild, budget 2–4 person-weeks of web rework even if screens stay the same.

findings.title: This repo is already a rebuild, and the same failure classes came back within 5 weeks
findings.detail:
90f0fad 'Initial clean rebuild foundation' (2026-08-18) replaced newfork (569 migrations, 3,094 commits). Its brief forbade kiosk and time tracking, required tenant and location scope in every check, ruled out SECURITY DEFINER shortcuts and asked for role test users. Today:
- 14 kiosk and time tables
- 639 SECURITY DEFINER functions (mostly harmless under service_role, but RLS is not the enforcement layer)
- no matrix test
- 38 red pgTAP files
This is the second-system effect, observed directly. The written rules were not the problem; nothing enforced them.
findings.fix_shape: Do not start a Gen 4. Turn the brief's rules into executable gates: the authorization-matrix test, pgTAP in CI, and structural catalog tests (for example: every actor function calls authorize(); no auth.uid() in service functions; no table without a grant plan).

findings.title: Some target-model violations are product rules or UI gates that no database rebuild fixes
findings.detail:
- Approved time off can be softened: conflict_rules accepts 'confirm' for approved_time_off (ConflictHandlingSettingsPage.tsx:31-35).
- Employee UI is closed to owner/admin/manager: App.tsx `roles={["employee"]}`, although the DB and API allow it.
- Time-off requests carry a single, employee-chosen location_id (NOT NULL), which conflicts with M2's 'time off belongs to the person'.
findings.fix_shape: A CHECK constraint (approved_time_off = 'block' only) and removal of that settings row; a web route change adding an 'Employee view' switch; M2's D4 (drop location_id, per-affected-location approval votes, 1–2 person-weeks).

implications_for_decision:
**Recommendation:** rebuild the authorization core, delete the parallel systems, collapse the legacy layers and squash the migrations. Do not do a full rebuild, and do not just consolidate in place.

Why not only consolidate in place: the unfinished switch in authorization style is a foundation flaw (45 claim bridges, 39 auth.uid() functions, 8 dead policies, 16 scope implementations, 15 API authorize() functions). Incremental consolidation left exactly this state after the 2026-09-08 hardening. It has to be replaced as one designed unit with a matrix test, not refactored helper by helper.

Why not a full rebuild:
- Class 1 (about 110 tables) is sound and already fits M2. The only schema changes are the time-off location field and the edit-lock index.
- No BL-070 bug needs a different domain model.
- The web is coupled to the RPC shapes through 168 files.
- Most of all, the last rebuild, which had a brief that prescribed exactly these controls, reproduced the same failures in 5 weeks.

Assumptions behind the estimates:
- A person-week is one week of the owner directing, reviewing and deciding. AI code generation is not the bottleneck: Gen 3 produced 66.8k migration lines in 5 weeks, 58% of them in 3 days.
- The scope model (M2) is decided first.
- Line Up is excluded.
- No data migration is needed.
- pgTAP is added to CI in every option.

**Targeted option (about 8–14 person-weeks):**
1. pgTAP in CI and deletion of retired-model tests: 0.5
2. The authorize() core, a single authorization style, and the matrix test: 3–5
3. Parallel systems (old availability, legacy Requests vs Shift Hub, kiosk/time): 2.5–3.5
4. Collapse the wrapper chains, remove legacy code, squash to a baseline: 1.5–2.5
5. M2 domain edits (G's D1–D7, including the data-losing edit lock): 1.5–3

**Full rebuild (about 13–24 person-weeks):**
1. Recreate class 1 with the new authorization: 5–8
2. Re-derive and re-verify decided behaviours (4,275 pgTAP assertions, 2,062 unit tests, 48 tasks, 63 backlog items, 142 docs, 24 decisions): 3–6
3. API rewire (288 routes, 193 RPCs): 1–2
4. Web rewire (439 schemas, 3,495 snake_case reads): 2–4
5. Stabilisation and regressions in areas that work today (document lifecycle, notification outbox, publish flow, two-location swap voting): 2–4

Hidden costs of a full rebuild:
- lost decisions
- a second set of new bugs
- MVP delay
- the owner's decision bandwidth spent re-deciding settled behaviour
- a demonstrated second-system effect

When a full rebuild would be right: only if the domain model had to change shape. For example, M1 with no multi-location employees, or a different tenancy unit. The current evidence does not point there.
